shape_hint: Hexagon nut with an integral round washer flange at the bottom (diameter dc, thin edge c, slightly conical top fillet r) so the side view is a hexagon body of height m with a wide flat flange disc at the base; optional radial serrations on the flange underside (DIN 6923 serrated version has the same dimensions).
notes: Only 3 source groups exist for these tables (fasteners.eu / boltport / engineersedge), found without web search (budget exhausted). ISO 4161:2012 style 2 coarse thread M5-M20; s_max values: M10 15 (not 16) and M12 18, M14 21, M16 24, M20 30. DIN 6923 additionally covers fine pitch M8x1, M10x1.25, M12x1.5 etc.; and the serrated version has identical dimensions. M10 uses s=15 mm (flange nuts differ from hexagon nuts).

problems: Record sources list only fasteners.eu, boltport, engineersedge. Boltport's flange-nut table has the same column set/layout/values as the fasteners.eu-derived torqbolt ISO 4161 page (differs only in M20 s_min 29.16 vs 29.67), so under the strict reading it is one cluster with fasteners.eu/torqbolt and the producer's list shows only 2 clusters. The third cluster comes from globalfastener DIN 6923-1983 / ISO 4161-1983 pages (not in the record; verified live) - add them to the sources.

Edition caveat: globalfastener's ISO 4161-1999 page gives m_min 7.64/9.64/11.57/18.7 for M8/M10/M12/M20 (record: 7.6/9.6/11.6/18.9 = DIN 6923, ISO 4161-1983, ASME B18.2.4.4M, fasteners.eu, Boltport, engineersedge). Record title 'DIN 6923 = EN 1661 = ISO 4161' is therefore not strictly true for m_min; label the table 'DIN 6923 / EN 1661' (ASME-compatible).

M14 e_min stays dropped: 23.36 on fasteners.eu, torqbolt, Boltport, globalfastener (3 pages of 2 strict clusters = FE+BP, GF) vs 23.35 engineersedge+torqbolt ASME page - only 2 strict clusters. M20 s_min column stays dropped (29.67 vs 29.16 split across editions).

Row label/semantics fine: coarse series only, M10 s=15 (flange nut, not 16/17), c_min = flange edge thickness min, dc_max flange diameter, dw_min bearing circle, s_max nominal=max, all read from headers.
